title: KV prefetch scheduling and warp-coop fusion notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures recent experiments and heuristics for reducing latency tail and token cost by combining request-level KV prefetch scheduling with warp-cooperative fused kernels. Focus is on: (1) prefetch budgeting and eviction heuristics for paged KV, (2) cross-request coalesced KV gathers for microbatches, and (3) design sketch for a fused matmul->attention->softmax kernel that can operate on partially-prefetched pages.

Summary of key ideas (TL;DR):
- Do lightweight asynchronous prefetch of hot KV pages into L2/shared memory with a small per-request credit so prefetching doesn't cause head-of-line load.
- Maintain a tiny per-client hot set counter (ring buffer of recent key ids) to decide pinning of pages across requests from same session.
- When microbatching, coalesce KV loads across requests in the microbatch by grouping page ids and issuing a single gather CTA per page to maximize bandwidth.
- Implement warp-cooperative gather for page entries: warps jointly traverse index lists and write contiguous chunks to shared memory to avoid random DRAM reads per thread.
- Provide a fallback path: if page not yet fetched, fused kernel can still run in a degraded path by issuing on-demand L2 loads with a higher latency; design kernels to be tolerant of missing pages (zero-fill + record miss for async fetch).

Experimental setup (short):
- Hardware: A100-40GB and H100-80GB instances.
- Models: decoder-only 30B and 70B working set (kv size trimmed to emulate long context 64k).
- Baseline: current paged-KV synchronous fetch per-token; microbatch size 8; token latency p99 ~ 420ms on 70B.
- New flow: async prefetch + warp-coop gather + fused attention kernel where possible. Microbatch 8.

Observed numbers (approx):
- 30B: p99 reduced from ~120ms -> ~90ms (25% improvement) when hot-set pinning enabled and coalesced gathers used.
- 70B: p99 reduced from ~420ms -> ~310ms (26% improvement), p95 improved less (~15%) because cold-first-token misses still expensive.
- Cost: marginal GPU cycles up (~4–8%) due to prefetch work but token-per-second throughput increased because reduced stalling.

Design details and heuristics:
1) Prefetch budgeting:
- Every request is given N prefetch credits (default N=3). Credits represent pages allowed to be issued async while the request is queued.
- Credits are consumed only for pages not already resident. Prefetch actions are best-effort and charged to the request for billing/telemetry.
- Unused credits can be donated to other requests on the same connection (helps bursty inputs).

2) Hot-set pinning:
- Maintain a per-session ring buffer (size 128 recent page ids). Frequency count (byte-sized counters) used to promote a page to 'pinned' state if seen >= M times in last window (M=3).
- Pinned pages are kept in a small LRU with TTL (milliseconds) and pinned pages are evicted last. Pin TTL tuned per model and workload.
- Rationale: chat-style sessions have locality; pinning reduces repeated misses.

3) Cross-request coalescing in microbatches:
- During microbatch assembly, build a mapping page_id -> list of (req_index, offset).
- For each page_id, launch a gather CTA that reads the page once and writes to shared workspace blocks used by each request.
- Synchronize with lightweight atomic counters per page to let per-request threads know when their segment is ready.
- Heuristic: only coalesce if page appears in >=2 requests in microbatch or if predicted fetch latency > threshold.

4) Warp-cooperative gather pattern:
- Each CTA assigned to one page. Threads in warp compute source indices and load 128B–512B aligned chunks into shared memory. Use 32-bit index tables to avoid 64-bit overhead.
- Reduce bank conflicts: interleave loads by lane map (lane_idx ^ (lane_idx >> 1)) to spread addresses across banks when accesses are strided.
- After shared stage, threads copy contiguous slices to per-request output buffers (aligned for subsequent fused kernel use).

5) Fused matmul->attention->softmax kernel considerations:
- Fusion benefit: eliminates intermediate global memory writes for QK and softmax vectors; reduces kernel launch overhead; enables use of shared memory for prefix reduction.
- Kernel must accept 'sparse-ready' inputs (some page entries zero-filled). Kernel keeps a miss bitmap and records misses in a per-request counter for later reissue.
- Mixed-precision accumulation: inputs in FP16/4, partial sums in FP32 for stability. Provide a compile-time path for FP32 accumulation when model flagged for high-sensitivity.

6) Degraded path and correctness:
- If fused kernel detects misses that exceed threshold (e.g., >10% of KV entries), mark request and re-run in non-fused, on-demand load mode to preserve correctness.
- Miss logging: capture page_id, token_index, latency, stack trace for replay to improve heuristics.

Microbenchmarks and tests to add:
- Synthetic generator that emits session sequences with controllable locality parameter to stress pinning heuristics. Measure p50/p95/p99 and prefetch bandwidth.
- Stress test: random access worst-case with TTL=0 to measure pure fetch bandwidth and eviction churn.
- Correctness fuzz: randomized zero-fill + replay to ensure fused kernel handles partial pages identically to baseline.

Open implementation questions and trade-offs:
- How many prefetch credits by default? N=3 worked in our tests but depends on model and network; need autoscale logic based on recent miss rates.
- Pin TTL: longer TTL helps sessions but increases memory pressure; need eviction thresholds by total pinned size per GPU.
- Prefetch interference: background prefetching can cause cache pollution for cold requests; propose strict budget and prioritized prefetch queue where requests pay credits.
- Coalescing latency: building page->request maps has overhead; cost-benefit break-even depends on average pages/request overlap. We should instrument overlap metric and enable coalescing only when overlap > 0.2.
- H100 differences: persistent L2 and new cache policies mean our L2-prefetch benefits change; add hardware-aware knobs.

Implementation sketch (pseudocode):
- On request enqueue:
    pages = compute_needed_pages(req)
    for p in pages:
        if is_resident(p): continue
        if req.credits > 0 and not background_queue_full():
            issue_async_prefetch(p, priority=req.priority)
            req.credits -= 1
        else:
            record_sync_needed(p)
- On microbatch assemble:
    map = build_page_to_requests(microbatch)
    for p, reqs in map.items():
        if len(reqs) >= 2 and predicted_latency(p) > L:
            launch_coalesced_gather(p, reqs)
        else:
            leave_to_individual_fetch(reqs)
- Fused kernel entry:
    inputs = per-request Q/K/V pointers (some segments 0)
    miss_bitmap = 0
    compute QK, apply masking
    if miss_ratio(miss_bitmap) > threshold: set degraded_flag
    else commit outputs

Telemetry and metrics to add:
- prefetch_credits_used_per_request (histogram)
- prefetched_pages_hit_rate
- coalesced_gathers_launched / microbatch
- avg_coalesced_page_size and per-page bandwidth
- fused_kernel_degraded_count and reasons

Rollout plan (staged):
- Canary in Dedicated (low traffic but stable sessions) with prefetch credits conservative (N=1), coalescing off. Collect telemetry.
- Enable coalescing for workloads with high session overlap (identified by telemetry).
- Gradually increase credits and enable pinning with strict per-GPU pinned-size cap.

TODOs / next steps:
- Implement microbatch map builder in C++ and benchmark overhead (Marta).
- Prototype warp-coop gather CTA and integrate with page cache API (Diego).
- Add fused-kernel miss-tolerant path and unit tests; add FP32-accum toggle (Evan).
- Run suite on H100 and record L2-prefetch characteristics (Aisha).

Unresolved research questions (for infra/research):
- Is pinning at page granularity best vs. finer-grained chunking? Chunking reduces wasted memory but increases index overhead.
- Can we build a lightweight ML predictor (per-model) to suggest prefetch targets vs. naive sliding-window?
- How to expose prefetch knobs to users safely (e.g., API flags) without opening cost surprises.

Notes to self: link to related experiments: PR 812 has a simple async prefetch impl; RT-2314 tracks paged-KV improvements; see Marta's sandbox for warp gather microbench (sandbox/gather-v6).

End.
